# Behaviour characterized from a legacy system runs the same on a second target
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #296, sha256:a486b55c4f1d864bffb10b2594816d008460c3bda9d7368f5433421092523571). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Draft
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (future; portability, slice 2 of 2)
- **Milestone:** M5 Synthesis (future)
- **Source:** board refinement of a product idea, split from card 295 on review. Because avowries generate code, the avowries that pin a legacy system's behaviour (card 295) can generate and check the same behaviour on another target, which makes them a bridge for a strangler-fig migration.
- **Depends on:** 295; 108 (a second target's specs project); a real, non-spike second adapter (no card yet: card 028 is its spike and informs risk only, it is not evidence of a supported adapter)
- **Story:** As Dana, I want the avowries that pin a legacy system's behaviour to generate and pass on a second target, so that I can move the system to another language without changing what it does.
- **One user-observable outcome:** Dana runs the captured avowries against the legacy system and the generated second target and sees, per behaviour, matched, adapter-required, or not captured.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given avowries captured by card 295 and two supported adapters, When each target is generated and run, Then both produce every captured returned, stored, emitted, responded or failed outcome, and the comparison fails if either omits or changes one. ZOMBIES: Z an empty suite cannot claim portability; O one outcome agrees; M all agree; B boundary values agree; I adapters are named; E captured failures agree; S regeneration is stable.
  2. Given a normalization rule per adapter (null against absent, number width, ordering), stated before any comparison runs, When outcomes are compared, Then only those rules apply, and a difference no rule covers fails. ZOMBIES: Z no rule needed; O one rule; M rules compose; B a value at the edge of a rule; I each rule is named in the report; E an uncovered difference fails; S rules cannot be added after a run.
  3. Given a behaviour that uses a platform side effect, When the target runs with its declared adapter, Then the report separates matched, adapter-required and not-captured behaviour, and fails if an adapter requirement is silently ignored. ZOMBIES: Z no side effect needs no adapter; O one requirement reported and exercised; M each reported separately; B platform limits explicit; I the adapter contract visible; E an adapter failure is observable; S timing or concurrency uncertainty is never reported as equivalence.
- **Flag decision:** ships behind the same default-off flag as card 295.
- **Limits:** generated targets still need platform adapters; avowries do not erase platform differences; only behaviour card 295 captured is carried.
- **Out of scope:** writing the second adapter itself; migrating a production system.

## Context

- Ranked after card 028 (the second adapter spike), at the end of the future work: it cannot start before card 295 and a real second adapter.
- Filed by the facilitator on 2026-11-04 from board refinement; split from card 295 on review.
